title: Jump Game
statement: You stand on the first cell of a row of non-negative numbers. A number tells you the longest jump you may make from that cell, and you may also jump any shorter distance. Decide whether you can land exactly on the last cell.

example.caption: From 2 you can reach the 3, and from the 3 you can reach past the end. Yes.

idea.sentence: Keep the farthest index you can reach. Every cell up to it is reachable, and a cell beyond it is not, so you only ever compare against that one number.

jargon.plain: Keep only the best summary (here: the farthest reach) instead of exploring every path.
You can land there by some sequence of allowed jumps.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a list of jump lengths, e.g. [2,3,1,1,4]

compare.bruteLabel: Try every jump from every cell

rows.name: Brute force search
rows.note: Explore every jump length from every reachable cell. Plain recursion without memory is exponential.

rows.name: Goal moves backward
rows.note: Same cost, scanned right to left.

fast.takeaway: Reachable cells form one unbroken stretch from index 0. One number, the end of that stretch, is all the state you need.

stages.title: Start with far = 0
stages.note: Before moving, index 0 is the only cell you can stand on.

stages.title: Is this cell reachable?
stages.note: If the index is beyond far, no earlier cell can land here. Stop with false.

stages.title: Stretch the reach
stages.note: From this cell you can reach index + value. Keep the larger of that and far.

stages.title: Goal inside reach
stages.note: If far covers the last index, the answer is true. You can stop early.

stages.title: Goal is the last cell
stages.note: The cell you still need to be able to reach.

stages.title: Pull the goal back
stages.note: If this cell can reach the goal, reaching this cell is enough. The goal moves here.

stages.title: Goal at index 0?
stages.note: If the goal was pulled all the way to the start, the answer is true.

edges.title: Single cell
edges.why: You already stand on the last cell. A zero here does not matter.

edges.title: Zero blocks the way
edges.why: Every path funnels into the 0 at index 3. From there far stays 3, and index 4 is beyond it.

edges.title: Zero at the start
edges.why: Index 0 can reach only itself. At index 1, 1 > far = 0, so you are stuck.

edges.title: A zero in the middle is harmless
edges.why: The first jump flies over both zeros and lands on the end. Zeros only matter if you must stand on them.

gotchas.text: Check i > far before using nums[i]. Standing on a cell you cannot reach would wrongly extend far.
Compare with i + nums[i], not nums[i] alone. The jump length is relative to the current cell.
The built-in max needs Go 1.21 or newer. On older versions write the if by hand.
Reading nums[i] past the end gives undefined, and Math.max with undefined is NaN. Every comparison with NaN is false, so far silently stops working. Keep i inside the array.

recap.key: Keep far, the farthest index reachable so far. If an index is beyond far you are stuck. Otherwise widen far with i + nums[i].
moves: For each i, if i > far return false
If far reaches the last index, return true
